title: Geo Point Field: Add Locations to Content Items

chapters.title: Geo Point Field: Add Locations to Content Items
chapters.subtitle: Give a content item a place on the map

steps.text: Some content belongs on a map, such as a shop, an office, or a venue. The Geo Point field stores that location on a content item. In this video, you enable the Spatial feature, add the field, and set a location.
A shop, an office, or a venue has a place. A Geo Point field keeps that place on the content item itself, as numbers that an editor can type or pick on a map.

The field stores two numbers: a latitude and a longitude. The Latitude box takes values from minus 90 to 90, and the Longitude box from minus 180 to 180. Both can stay empty unless the field is required.

The editor comes in two forms. Standard shows the two boxes, and Leaflet editor adds a map, where a click fills in the boxes. The map background comes from OpenStreetMap, so the browser needs internet access.
Let's open Tools, Features, and search for Spatial. Its row lists the features it depends on directly: Content Types and Lucene.
Let's select Enable. A message confirms that the feature Spatial was enabled. Lucene is enabled with it, because Spatial depends on it.
Let's open Design, Content Definition, Content Types. We add the field to the Page content type, so we select Edit on its row.
Under Fields, we select Add Field. We type Location as the Display Name, and the Technical Name follows from it. Then we choose Geo Point Field as the Field Type.
We select Save & Configure. The field's settings include Required, which makes both coordinates mandatory, and Hint, which shows help text under the Latitude and Longitude boxes.
Each box is labeled only Latitude or Longitude, so a hint tells editors which location the field holds. Let's check Required and write a hint.
Further down the settings page, the editor list offers Standard, with two number boxes, and Leaflet editor, which adds a map. We choose Leaflet editor and select Save.
Back on the Page content type, the Location field is listed as a Geo Point Field, with a Leaflet badge for its editor.

chapters.title: Set a location
chapters.subtitle: Click the map or type the numbers

steps.text: Let's open Content, Content Items, select New, and choose Page. We type Find Us as the title.
We scroll down below the page content. The field shows a Latitude box, a Longitude box, and a map, with the hint under each box.
Clicking the map chooses a place. The boxes fill in with six decimal places, and a marker with a popup shows the point.
To be exact, we type the values ourselves, and the marker follows what we type. Let's enter the coordinates of our shop.
We select Publish. A message confirms that your Page has been published, and the list shows it.

chapters.title: Check the result
chapters.subtitle: In the editor and on the site

steps.text: We select Edit on the Find Us row. Because the field has values, the map opens centered on the saved location, with a marker.
Back in the list, we select View. The site shows the location as text: the latitude, a comma, and the longitude, each with six decimal places.

The location is stored with the content item and shown on the site as text. When the content type belongs to a Lucene index and the field's setting Include this element in the index is checked, developers can search by area or by distance.
